transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I guess what brings me in is this constant feeling of being restless, like I’m wound too tight most of the time. It’s not even always dramatic, but it’s there — like I can’t fully settle into my own body.

I notice it in situations where I really should be calm, like sitting through a planning meeting at work, or even doing things that are supposed to relax me. I paint sometimes, and even then I’ll feel this internal buzzing, like I need to shift around or get up or do something else. And yoga — I mean, yoga is supposed to be calming, right? But I’ll be there trying to breathe and hold a pose and I still feel like I can’t quite come down. It’s uncomfortable, and it’s been bothering me enough that I thought I should finally talk to someone about it.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about different things in your life, like work, relationships, or health, even when there isn’t a clear reason to be concerned?

I don’t think so, not in the way you’re describing. I mean, I have normal worries, I guess — if there’s something actually going on at work or a bill or some family thing, I’ll think about it — but I wouldn’t say I’m sitting around worrying about my health or relationships or everything all at once for no clear reason.

It’s more like… I can feel unsettled without there being a specific worry attached to it, if that makes sense. Like my body is on, but my mind isn’t necessarily spinning through “what if” thoughts. So I’m not sure I’d call it worry, exactly.
Do you often find yourself needing to move, like you can't sit still for very long, even when you're not particularly anxious or stressed?

Yes, definitely. That’s actually probably the clearest way it shows up for me. It’s like I have this constant restless feeling, like I’m wound too tight, and I can’t quite settle into whatever I’m doing.

It happens even when I’m not especially upset or stressed. Like in a planning meeting at work, I’ll be sitting there knowing I’m supposed to just listen and take things in, but inside I feel like I need to shift, move, adjust myself, something. And it’s not because I’m panicking or worried about the meeting — it’s more physical than that.

Even with things that should be calming, it’s there. If I’m painting, which I normally enjoy, I can still feel kind of… buzzing inside, like I can’t fully relax into it. And yoga is probably the funniest example, because the whole point is to slow down and be still, but I’ll be there trying to breathe and hold the pose, and I still feel like I want to crawl out of my own skin a little. So yes, sitting still for very long is hard for me, even when there isn’t some obvious stress causing it.

Do you find this restlessness and need to move happens in different parts of your life — like at home, at work, or when you’re with friends — or is it mostly in certain situations like meetings or when you’re trying to relax?

It’s definitely in more than one setting. Meetings are just the easiest example because they’re so obvious — like I’m sitting there at work, and everyone else seems able to just sit normally and listen, and I’m shifting around or feeling like I need to move even if I’m trying not to show it.

But it’s not only work. It happens at home too, even when I’m doing something I actually like. Painting is a good example because I want that to be relaxing, and sometimes it is, but there’s still this feeling underneath like I’m wound too tight, like I can’t fully settle into it. I’ll be trying to focus on the colors or the brush strokes, and part of me still feels physically restless.

And yoga too — which feels ridiculous to say because it’s supposed to help with exactly that — but even there, when I’m supposed to be calm and breathing and holding still, I can feel that buzzing inside, like I need to shift or move or just do something. So no, it’s not just meetings. It shows up in different parts of my life, especially any time I’m expected to be still or calm.
Do you find it hard to stay focused on tasks or conversations, like your mind drifting off or getting easily distracted, even when you’re trying to pay attention?

Yes, that does happen. I’ll be trying to pay attention, and I can even be looking right at the person, like I’m listening, but then I realize I didn’t actually take in everything they said.

It happens at work in sourcing meetings, for example. Someone will be explaining something or asking me a question, and I’m sitting there looking at them, nodding along, and then suddenly I catch only the last few words and think, wait, what did they actually ask me? And then I have to say, “Sorry, can you repeat that?” which is embarrassing, especially because it looks like I should have heard it.

It can happen at home too, like at the dinner table. Someone will ask me something, and I’ll realize a few seconds later that I only caught the tail end of it. It’s not that I’m trying to ignore them. I’m genuinely trying to listen, but my attention just sort of slips off for a moment, and then I have to backtrack.
Do you often find it hard to stay focused on tasks or conversations, even when you’re trying to pay attention, like your mind drifting off or getting easily distracted?

Yes, I do. It’s that thing where I can look like I’m paying attention — I’m making eye contact, I’m nodding, I’m not doing anything obviously distracted — but then a few seconds later I realize I didn’t actually absorb what they said.

It happens in sourcing meetings at work, which is awkward because those are exactly the times I’m supposed to be taking in details. Someone will ask me something or explain a point, and I’ll catch maybe the last part of the sentence, but not the lead-up, so I’m left trying to piece it together from context. Sometimes I have to say, “Sorry, can you repeat that?” and I feel embarrassed because from the outside it probably looks like I just wasn’t listening.

And it happens at home too, like at the dinner table. Someone can be talking directly to me, and I’ll realize I only caught the tail end of what they said. It’s not intentional, and I’m not trying to be rude. I really can be trying to listen, but my mind just kind of slips away for a moment, and then I’m behind.
Do you often find yourself acting on impulse, like blurting things out before thinking them through, interrupting others, or doing things without considering the consequences?

Yes, I do, though I’d say it’s not like I’m doing wildly risky things or anything dramatic. It’s more verbal, mostly. I’ll jump in too fast.

At work, especially during vendor negotiations, I’ll sometimes answer before the person has actually finished the question. In my head I think I know where they’re going, so I start responding, and then a second later they add some qualifier or condition that changes the meaning. Then I realize, oh, I answered the wrong version of the question. It’s embarrassing because in those conversations the wording really matters, and I don’t want to seem careless or like I’m not listening.

It happens in STEM mentoring sessions too. A student or mentee will be asking something, and I’ll think, “Oh, I know this one,” and I jump in with an answer before they’re done. Then they finish the question and I realize there was an important detail I missed. I usually try to correct myself, like, “Wait, sorry, I jumped ahead,” but I can feel that I moved before I really thought it through.

So yes, it’s usually blurting or interrupting with an answer too soon, rather than pausing and letting the whole question land first.
